mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 showed sustained growth over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% in the last two months signals a supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as supply chain disruptions and reduced output impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO declined by more than 1% in the last two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.3% in the last month, it indicates an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS was above 4% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in the last month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2%, signals a tightening labor market, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as strong employment data boosts consumer confidence and spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 300,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 300,000 and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the last month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts by more than 10% in the last three months indicates a strong demand for housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the housing sector's strength reflects broader economic health.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 10% in the last three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in the last two months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as reduced spending impacts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where RSAFS decreased by more than 1% in the last two months.
